<?php

/**
 * Bench Dogs release-stage policy for the shared Partial Fulfillment writer.
 *
 * This class returns plain data and never saves an Opportunity. The shared
 * package validates the stage/probability and remains the sole writer.
 *
 * DECISION 87(b): CLASSIFICATION IS DERIVED FROM NATIVE ROWS, NOT LOOKED UP IN
 * A MIRROR.
 *
 * Up to rc28 this opened `bd01_erp_quote_quotes`, resolved exactly one mirror
 * header, walked `bd01_erp_quote_lines`, built a line_num -> prototype|production
 * map, and then joined each ordered native Product back onto it through
 * `bd_erp_line_num`. Five reads, four of which could go ambiguous, and one of
 * which - the join key - is populated on 4 of 473 rows.
 *
 * None of that is needed. `_is_prototype()` is a PURE FUNCTION of two inputs
 * that both survive natively and are both written by core's own lane:
 *
 *     benchdogs-erp-custom/connector_ext_benchdogs/transformers/quotes.py:119-124
 *       _PROTOTYPE_PART = re.compile(r"(^|[-_])PROTO", re.IGNORECASE)
 *       def _is_prototype(part_num, line_desc):
 *           return bool(_PROTOTYPE_PART.search(part_num)
 *                       or "prototype" in line_desc.lower())
 *
 * part_num is `Products.mft_part_num` and line_desc is `Products.description`.
 * The regex below is that one, ported character for character: same alternation,
 * same anchor set, same case-insensitivity, same substring fallback on the
 * description. It is applied to the SAME strings the connector applied it to, so
 * this is a re-derivation rather than a re-implementation. Measured on Bench:
 * 11 of 473 rungs classify as prototype, on 11 quotes, ALL ELEVEN matched by the
 * part number and none by the description alone.
 *
 * WHY IT IS NOT A STORED FIELD. A stored copy would freeze a classification a
 * person can later contradict by editing the part number, and the connector
 * would be its only writer - so a hand-built release would carry no
 * classification at all. Deriving costs one preg_match per ordered line.
 *
 * WHY VALUATION DOES NOT NEED THIS AT ALL. Under 87(b)'s per-GROUP rule the
 * prototype is its own mft_part_num group and carries its own pin, so
 * ErpQuoteOpportunityContribution sums it like any other pinned rung and never
 * asks what kind of line it is. THE ONLY CONSUMER OF "is this a prototype" IS
 * STAGE CLASSIFICATION, which is this file.
 *
 * WHAT THAT REMOVES, stated because removing a refusal is a behaviour change:
 * the "Ambiguous ERP quote revision", "ERP quote line identity is ambiguous" and
 * "Ordered Quote line has no unambiguous ERP quote-line identity" throws are
 * gone. Every one of them guarded a JOIN that no longer happens. The one
 * remaining refusal is the one that is about the release itself - no committed
 * line is visible - and it is unchanged.
 *
 * ALSO GONE: the "Multiple prototype lines make release stage ambiguous" throw.
 * On the mirror, two prototype lines meant a shape nobody could read. Under
 * per-group grouping, two prototype rungs are simply two groups, and neither the
 * valuation nor this classification is ambiguous about them: production still
 * outranks prototype, exactly as before.
 *
 * WHAT IS UNCHANGED: production outranks prototype; the two stage/probability
 * pairs; the snapshot discipline below (Order Selected Lines loads `products`
 * before it stamps the ordered line, so each Product is re-read outside
 * BeanFactory's request cache); and the fact that this class writes nothing.
 */
class ErpOpportunityReleaseStagePolicy
{
    /**
     * The connector's own prototype part-number pattern, ported verbatim from
     * `_PROTOTYPE_PART` (Python `re.IGNORECASE` -> PHP `i`). Do not "tidy" the
     * alternation: `(^|[-_])` is what stops `NOPROTOTYPING-1` matching, and it
     * is the difference between a rung that closes on its own and one that does
     * not.
     */
    private const PROTOTYPE_PART = '/(^|[-_])PROTO/i';

    /**
     * @return array{sales_stage: string, probability: int}|null
     */
    public function resolve(SugarBean $quote): ?array
    {
        // The same applicability gate ErpQuoteOpportunityContribution opens
        // with, and for the same reason: a Sugar-authored quote is not a Bench
        // Dogs release and this policy has nothing to say about it. Null means
        // "not applicable" and leaves the shared writer's own stage handling
        // alone; it is not a refusal.
        if (trim((string) ($quote->erp_sync_key ?? '')) === '') {
            return null;
        }

        if (!$quote->load_relationship('products')
            || !$quote->products
            || !is_object($quote->products)
        ) {
            throw new UnexpectedValueException('Quote line items unavailable for release stage');
        }

        // Order Selected Lines loads this relationship before it stamps the
        // selected Product. SugarBean::retrieve() refreshes the Quote fields,
        // but it does not discard an already-loaded Link2 bean snapshot. A
        // getBeans() here therefore observed erp_ordered=false after the order
        // had actually succeeded on QA. Resolve relationship IDs, then read
        // each Product outside BeanFactory's cache so release policy observes
        // the committed row rather than the action's pre-order snapshot.
        $productIds = $quote->products->get();
        if (!is_array($productIds)) {
            throw new UnexpectedValueException('Quote line-item identities unavailable for release stage');
        }

        $hasPrototype = false;
        $hasProduction = false;
        foreach ($productIds as $productId) {
            $product = BeanFactory::retrieveBean(
                'Products',
                (string) $productId,
                ['use_cache' => false]
            );
            if (!$product || empty($product->id)) {
                throw new UnexpectedValueException('Quote line item unavailable for release stage');
            }
            if (!empty($product->deleted) || empty($product->erp_ordered)) {
                continue;
            }
            if (self::isPrototype($product)) {
                $hasPrototype = true;
            } else {
                $hasProduction = true;
            }
        }

        if ($hasProduction) {
            return [
                'sales_stage' => 'Partial Production Closed',
                'probability' => 90,
            ];
        }
        if ($hasPrototype) {
            return [
                'sales_stage' => 'Prototype Closed',
                'probability' => 80,
            ];
        }

        throw new UnexpectedValueException(
            'No committed Quote line is visible for Bench release-stage policy'
        );
    }

    /**
     * `_is_prototype(part_num, line_desc)`, ported. Public so a caller that
     * needs the same classification reads it from here rather than re-typing
     * the regex - there must be exactly one copy of this rule in the package.
     */
    public static function isPrototype(SugarBean $line): bool
    {
        $part = (string) ($line->mft_part_num ?? '');
        $description = (string) ($line->description ?? '');

        return preg_match(self::PROTOTYPE_PART, $part) === 1
            || strpos(strtolower($description), 'prototype') !== false;
    }
}
